title: Vision Transformers for Dense Prediction
layout_note: The overview is an upside-down U. A gridded input photo at bottom-left goes right through Embed into a token grid, then up a column of four Transformer blocks; from the connector above each Transformer a horizontal rung runs right to a Reassemble box (subscripts 4, 8, 16, 32 from bottom to top) and on into a Fusion box. The Fusion column runs back down, top to bottom, through Head into the output depth map at bottom-right, so input and output sit level with each other at the bottom. Two detail panels follow to the right: Reassemble_s (centre) and Fusion (right).
grouping: Three untitled panels side by side, split by two thin full-height black vertical rules; the overview is the widest. Inside the overview there are no containers: parts are grouped by colour family per column (slate blue-grey Transformers, green Reassemble boxes, purple Fusion boxes, with a single olive Embed and a single rust Head). Each detail panel puts its steps in one large rounded light-tinted container whose tint matches that module's overview colour (pale green for Reassemble_s, pale lavender for Fusion), titled in bold black in the container's bottom corner. In the Reassemble_s panel the input tokens and the output feature block sit outside, above the container, with arrows entering and leaving it.
shapes_depth: Overview blocks are flat rounded rectangles with a small corner radius, solid muted fills, white sans-serif labels and no shadows; boxes in a column share one size. Detail-panel step boxes are smaller rounded rectangles with a pale fill of the module's hue, a thin darker outline of that hue and black labels. Tokens are drawn as small 3-D diagonal prisms in a 3 x 4 grid, orange, with one extra red-orange prism at the end of the middle row; after Read the same grid reappears in mustard yellow without the extra prism. Concatenate yields a small yellow 3-D cuboid, and the Reassemble_s output is a large light-orange 3-D cuboid. Fusion's merge is a small circled plus. Arrows are thin black lines with filled heads, with right-angle elbows where the rungs leave the Transformer column. Module scale is written as a subscript in the label (Reassemble_32, Resample_s, Resample_0.5). The input is a photo with white grid lines over it for patches; the output is a greyscale depth map.
proposed_highlight: The two proposed modules, Reassemble and Fusion, each get a distinct saturated hue in the overview (green, purple) against the neutral slate of the Transformer backbone, and each is expanded in its own detail panel whose rounded container repeats that hue as a pale tint and carries the module name in bold. No legend or connector lines tie overview to detail; the shared hue and name do it. The overview's concrete scales (4, 8, 16, 32) become the generic subscript s in the detail panel's title.
lesson: Each proposed module keeps one hue across panels, a solid fill for its box in the overview and a pale tint of the same hue for its detail panel's rounded container, so the reader matches block to expansion without a legend or callout lines.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2103.13413); the venue's year was not verified. Venue ICCV as recorded from Semantic Scholar. The paper is dense prediction (depth shown) on natural images; it is carded under medical-imaging only as a mechanism reference for a transformer-encoder segmentation figure. Panels carry no letters or titles; the caption names them Left/Center/Right and states the colour coding (orange tokens, red readout token, green reassemble, purple fusion). The input photo and the output depth map are recorded as embedded images by refs crop, so they are excluded from the palette and counted in photo_share.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: monocular depth estimation and semantic segmentation

core.what: an overview at left (a column of four Transformer blocks tapped by rungs into Reassemble_4..32 and a column of Fusion boxes) plus two detail panels for Reassemble_s and Fusion, each in a rounded container tinted like its overview boxes, separated by full-height vertical rules

relations.form: an upside-down U in the overview: photo patches enter bottom-left, Embed goes right, the Transformer column climbs upward, rungs go right, the Fusion column descends to Head and a real depth map at bottom right
four horizontal rungs from the Transformer column at four heights, each ending in a Reassemble box with its scale subscript (4, 8, 16, 32) and a Fusion box beside it, so scale is read by height
the Fusion column chains top-down, each Fusion box taking the box above plus its own Reassemble output from the left; the Fusion detail draws this as a side input joining at a circled plus
the green-tinted Reassemble_s panel and purple-tinted Fusion panel match the green Reassemble and purple Fusion boxes of the overview, with no connecting lines
the input photo is cut into a visible grid of patches and tokens are drawn as rows of orange 3-D sticks with one red readout token, reassembled into 3-D feature blocks

channels.colour: module type: slate = Transformer, green = Reassemble, purple = Fusion, brown = Head/Embed; token colour (orange sticks, red readout, yellow after Read) marks data kind, but orange also fills the final reassembled feature block, so orange means both 'transformer token' and 'output feature map'
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = operation, 3-D stick = token, 3-D block = image-like feature map, photo = input/output
channels.line: one style: thin black arrows for data flow
channels.frame: full-height vertical rules separate overview from details; a tinted rounded container = the inside of one module

quality.strengths: Zoom is bound by colour alone and the overview's geometry encodes scale by rung height, so the multi-resolution taps read without labels; tokens and features are drawn as data (patch grid, 3-D sticks with a distinct readout token, 3-D blocks) between the operations that make them; all paths are short and orthogonal.
quality.weaknesses: The detail panels are untitled at the top (names sit bottom-right inside the tint) and the overview has no panel label; orange covers both tokens and the reassembled output volume; the Fusion detail's two unlabeled entry arrows do not say which comes from Reassemble and which from the previous Fusion.

insights.structure: Three untitled panels split by thin full-height vertical rules: an overview at left (a column of four Transformer blocks with rungs out to Reassemble_4..32 boxes and a column of Fusion boxes), then a Reassemble_s detail panel and a Fusion detail panel each in a rounded tinted container.
insights.data: The input is a real photo cut into a grid of patches, tokens are orange 3-D sticks (one red readout token), the reassembled feature is a yellow 3-D block, and the output is a real grey depth map.
insights.emphasis: Each module has one colour family (slate Transformer, green Reassemble, purple Fusion) and its detail panel's container takes a pale tint of the same colour, binding overview box to zoom without any connecting lines.
insights.flow: An upside-down U: input enters bottom-left, goes right through Embed and up the Transformer column, rungs go right to Reassemble and Fusion, then down the Fusion column through Head to the depth map at bottom-right.
insights.avoid: Detail panels have no explicit link to the overview other than colour, and the card's domain tag 'medical-imaging' does not match this natural-image figure.

arrangement.units: three panels separated by thin vertical rules: the overview (no container) and two module details, each detail in a rounded container tinted to match its module colour with a bold title in the bottom corner
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo cut into a patch grid at bottom-left
arrangement.shared: module colour families reused between overview boxes and detail containers
